Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Acute 4-day illness with sore throat, rhinorrhoea/nasal congestion, evolving dry cough, low-grade fever (now resolved), night sweats, myalgias, headaches, mild exertional dyspnoea.  
• No red-flag symptoms (no chest pain, no dyspnoea at rest, no rash, no significant GI/urinary symptoms).  
• Otherwise healthy man, occasional cigar smoking, lives alone, mild work stress.

Working diagnosis  
• Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold) – high likelihood based on typical symptom progression and improvement (supported by DDx).  

Considerations  
• Influenza – medium likelihood given systemic symptoms; monitor for persistence or worsening.  
• COVID-19 (mild) – medium likelihood; consider testing if clinically indicated or symptoms worsen.  

Management  
• Symptomatic treatment: continue paracetamol/ibuprofen PRN, maintain hydration, rest; advised 1–2 days off work.  
• Safety-net advice: return earlier for high fever, increasing breathlessness, chest pain, or lack of improvement within 7 days.  
• Follow-up planned next week if not improved.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Advised adequate rest, hydration, gradual return to exercise post-recovery; reinforcement of smoking reduction and moderation of alcohol.  
- Patient health goals and priorities: Recover from current illness; resume normal activities.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): None today; consider Quitline if cigar use increases.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Review in ≤ 7 days if no improvement or sooner if red-flag symptoms occur.

- Mental health support or counselling referral: Not required at present; patient aware of availability.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not indicated.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified: Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening: Not indicated today.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected: Not indicated.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health: Not indicated.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection – High: Classic progression of sore throat → rhinorrhoea → dry cough with self-limiting course.  
2. Influenza – Medium: Abrupt systemic symptoms (fever, myalgias, headaches) align; fever duration shorter than typical.  
3. COVID-19 (mild) – Medium: Overlapping URI features plus night sweats and exertional breathlessness; consider epidemiology and testing.
